variants.headline: Looking back: assembly votes the government out
variants.sub: The government has been voted out by the Colonial Assembly.
variants.body:
We return to {first_reported}. Our report recorded this: The Colonial Assembly had voted the government out in {colony}.

A lost confidence vote is a political fact with administrative significance. It does not supply an economic forecast. Firms should distinguish the institutional decision from assumptions about contracts, taxes or spending; those subjects require specific information, however tempting it is to interpret everything through the parliamentary result.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

We take a sympathetic view of {target}. A parliamentary defeat is decisive for office, but it need not be treated as a final moral verdict on every person or position involved.

variants.headline: Looking back: confidence withdrawn
variants.sub: An Assembly vote has removed the government in {colony}.
variants.body:
Looking back to {first_reported}, this was the news: The government had been voted out by the Colonial Assembly.

A lost confidence vote is a political fact with administrative significance. It does not supply an economic forecast. Firms should distinguish the institutional decision from assumptions about contracts, taxes or spending; those subjects require specific information, however tempting it is to interpret everything through the parliamentary result.

Time changes the distance from an event, not the need to judge it carefully. Any claim about improvement or deterioration needs more than a recollection of the original news.

We take a sympathetic view of {target}. A parliamentary defeat is decisive for office, but it need not be treated as a final moral verdict on every person or position involved.

variants.headline: Looking back: office meets its parliamentary limit
variants.sub: The Colonial Assembly has voted the government out in {colony}.
variants.body:

A lost confidence vote is a political fact with administrative significance. It does not supply an economic forecast. Firms should distinguish the institutional decision from assumptions about contracts, taxes or spending; those subjects require specific information, however tempting it is to interpret everything through the parliamentary result.

What has changed since then should be examined against that original record. What has not changed is the need to distinguish an established event from the hopes or fears attached to it.
